No 'How are you today?' and no agenda statement — jumped straight from 'How can I help you' into date and pricing with no roadmap for the call
Never recapped or confirmed details on file even though he told the customer 'I have it' regarding name and phone number

No 'pricing is super simple' framing — pricing was delivered reactively, one number at a time, only when the customer asked

Estimate variables never explained: stairs/elevator, walk distance, specialty items, drive time, assembly/disassembly

Contradicted himself on the estimate build-up — first said 'six hours to pack and seven hours to move' for $2,652, then said 'seven hours for packing and six hours for moving' for $2,953, with no clear explanation of what changed
Answered 'That is correct. That is correct. No, we cannot.' to a compound question — left the customer to sort out which answer applied to what

top_strength: Pricing math held together under a customer who kept re-asking the same question different ways — Jules correctly separated the weekday $204 and weekend $222 rates, flagged that Friday counts as weekend, and consistently held the line that packing plus moving a full two-bedroom is a two-day job rather than caving to the customer's repeated attempts to compress it into one. He also stated 'no deposit' cleanly and gave his name and direct hours at the end.
coaching_note: This call was 14 minutes of the customer interviewing Jules instead of Jules running a sales call — every single piece of information came out only because the customer asked for it. The single highest-value fix: when the customer said 'it is too much for us to close on the house' and spent four minutes trying to figure out Thursday-vs-Friday logistics, that was the moment to run the Save Your Ass prep speech (consolidate the kids' toys and loose drawer items, take a carload yourself, photos off the walls) and explain the clock (2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments after). That answer directly solves his stated problem — it lowers his bill and shortens his day — and it costs 90 seconds. Instead he got silence, and then 'we do not do pencil booking.' Pair that with getting his name in the first 30 seconds and using it: he offered 'my name is Ari' unprompted and Jules never said it once.
phone_presence_notes: Polite bookends ('my pleasure, I hope you have a great day') but zero name use, almost no affirmations beyond repeated 'that is correct' and 'sounds good', and clear stress and cost cues from the customer went entirely unacknowledged.
audio_review_reason: Phone presence scored 2 — transcript reads flat and transactional with heavy repetition of 'that is correct', but the customer had a strong accent and the line broke up at least once ('Sir broke up'), so audio should confirm whether this is genuinely flat delivery or a transcript artifact of a difficult connection.
